questions.stem: In case 1796 on 10.40.2.0/24, an analyst considers how a packet network works. Which explanation of sequence numbers would a careful engineer give?
questions.subject: COMPUTER_NETWORKS

questions.explanation: Because IP packets can be reordered or duplicated, TCP attaches a byte-oriented sequence number to the data so the receiver can place it correctly and notice missing ranges. Acknowledgements use the same numbering to report the next expected byte. This is independent of the order in which routers happened to forward the underlying packets. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
questions.hint: Ask how the receiver can tell two segments apart after reordering.
questions.learningObjective: identify and explain sequence numbers using a packet-level scenario
